title: Has Machine Learning for Systems Reached an Inflection Point?
problem: It is unclear whether ML-for-systems research has reached a tipping point analogous to AlexNet in 2012, where ML transitions from one of many competing approaches to the dominant methodology. The paper investigates whether systems research has arrived at or is approaching that inflection point.
motivation: Prior ML-for-systems work has shown isolated wins but has not achieved the comprehensive, field-wide dominance that ML achieved in computer vision and NLP, raising the question of whether the field is now at a structural turning point.
method: The paper is a position/vision paper that surveys the trajectory of ML-for-systems research across sub-domains (scheduling, compilers, storage, networking, etc.), comparing their adoption curves to known ML inflection points in other fields. It evaluates evidence of maturation indicators such as production deployments, benchmark standardization, and displacement of handcrafted heuristics.
key_novelty: Frames ML-for-systems progress as an inflection-point analysis, drawing a structured parallel to AlexNet's transformation of computer vision to assess readiness and remaining barriers.
contributions: Systematic survey of ML-for-systems research trajectories across multiple systems sub-domains.
Identification of indicators that distinguish pre- and post-inflection-point phases in ML adoption.
Analysis of remaining gaps (data, benchmarks, deployment pipelines) that may delay a full inflection point.
limitations: Not discussed; paper is a position/vision piece without empirical experiments.
